solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flowers thrive around spring and summer primarily

indicators.note: around says the first word wraps itself about the letters that follow
primarily asks for only the opening letter of the season named before it

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for spring

explanation.surface: Garden plants doing well as the warm seasons arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring here is just its abbreviation, not a season to be defined; both seasons supply a single letter each.
explanation.definitionFit: Blossom is the mass of blooms on a tree or shrub, so it can stand for flowers as a noun.

clue.text: A son tucked into cream — most disgraceful!

indicators.note: tucked into means the first pair of letters is placed inside the word for cream

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
the cream is the best of anything

explanation.surface: Someone shocked that a boy has been put into the dairy cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Base means low or ignoble in character, so the superlative is the most shameful or contemptible.

clue.text: Boy's terrified — just a bit pink?

indicators.note: just a bit says only part of the run of words is wanted, lying inside it

blocks.note: the letters run across the first two words

explanation.surface: A frightened lad has gone slightly pale or pink.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: oyster pink is a named shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Oyster is a pale pinkish-grey colour name, as in oyster pink paint, hence a kind of pink.

clue.text: Plant appetite-suppressing drug? Fancy that!

blocks.note: amphetamine, a street drug that kills hunger

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some plant could curb your appetite like a diet pill.
explanation.walkthrough: Speed is slang for amphetamine, which suppresses appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a small wild flower with blue petals, a common European herbaceous species.

clue.text: What could make a cinema sell lots of bits and pieces?

indicators.note: asks what the following letters could be rebuilt into, inviting a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Asking what would help a picture house shift its odds and ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Miscellanea is a collection of assorted items or writings, an assortment of odds and ends.

clue.text: Clangers? Hard work must be restricted for servants

indicators.note: the hard work is restricted, held within the bounds of the clangers

blocks.note: H for hard, as on pencils
an opus, a piece of work

explanation.surface: Servants whose mistakes are punished by limits on their hard labour.
explanation.walkthrough: Clangers looks like blunders (British slang for gaffes), but here means bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellhops are hotel porters who carry luggage and run errands, a kind of uniformed attendant.

clue.text: Wardrobe malfunction exposes it? A mistake!

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for a breast, revealed when clothing slips

explanation.walkthrough: Wardrobe malfunction is the jokey phrase for clothing accidentally revealing too much.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word is informal both for a woman's breast and for a silly error or gaffe.

clue.text: Intellectual studies? Brits are all at sea

indicators.note: being all at sea is being confused, so those letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A dig that British people are bewildered by academic learning.
explanation.definitionFit: The liberal arts are university subjects such as literature, philosophy and history, studied for general intellectual development.

clue.text: Barnet worker in hotel bearing furniture

blocks.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
an air is a manner or bearing
a dresser is a piece of furniture with shelves

explanation.surface: Someone at a hotel carrying a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), and also a district of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser is the person whose job is cutting and styling hair, so a worker on your barnet.

clue.text: Obstinate and conceited, wanting power for British

indicators.note: asks for one abbreviation to stand in place of another inside the word for conceited

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Describing a stubborn, vain person who wants power instead of nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: The B at the front of BIGHEADED is swapped for P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig-headed means stubbornly refusing to change your mind, the same idea as stubborn.

clue.text: Composer needing help with English language initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: to give a hand is to help
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A foreign composer needing help with English when he first arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting surface: the German-born composer settled in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel was the German-born Baroque composer of Messiah who worked mostly in England.

clue.text: A knight works to secure Eastern islands

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one word encloses the next

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for knight
tills the soil, works the land
E is the abbreviation for Eastern

explanation.surface: A knight's deeds protecting some islands in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: Works is a verb here: to till is to work the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antilles are the island chain of the Caribbean, the Greater and Lesser groups of the West Indies.

clue.text: Briefly communicate help before winching to safety?

blocks.note: first meaning: write a short note to somebody
second meaning, taken literally: lower a rope to a person in trouble

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading of the idiom: a rescuer lowers a rope before hauling someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to send a brief letter or message, a quick informal written contact.

clue.text: Actual mistake made by keyboarder

blocks.note: second meaning: a printers' word for a typing error

explanation.walkthrough: In publishing a typo is traditionally called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means true to the plain sense, and as a noun it is the printing trade's term for a typo.

clue.text: Game faced with temporary stoppage — one brings two sides together

explanation.surface: A match halted for a while before two teams can meet.
explanation.walkthrough: Faced with puts the stoppage in front of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspension bridge spans a river or gorge, joining its two banks, hung from cables.

clue.text: A solicitor holding sealed case finally dined in restaurant?

indicators.note: holding means the solicitor keeps one letter within his grasp
finally keeps just the very end of the words in front of it

blocks.note: one who solicits custom, not a lawyer
last letter of case; a sealed case is an envelope, which ends the same way

explanation.surface: A lawyer with a sealed document case went for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Solicitor looks like a British lawyer but means a tout touting for business.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat out is to have a meal at a restaurant rather than at home; the past tense matches dined.

clue.text: Crouch with head hidden having come down to produce some poetry

indicators.note: with its head hidden, the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: to rain is to come down from the sky

explanation.surface: Someone hunched over, hiding their face, after a fall, writing verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A quatrain is a stanza of four lines, so a small piece of poetry.

clue.text: Notice one horse going round less agitated

indicators.note: going round says the horse forms a circle about the other pieces

explanation.surface: Seeing a horse circle round makes the rider calmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something steadied has been calmed, made more stable and less shaken, so rendered less agitated.

clue.text: Squandering half away? Reminder given

indicators.note: half away means one half of the word goes, leaving only its front

explanation.surface: Someone who wasted half their money is given a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the eight letters of PRODIGAL, the back four go.
explanation.definitionFit: A prod is a nudge or prompt that jogs someone into action, a gentle reminder.

clue.text: A potential point-scorer for the team?

definitions.text: A potential point-scorer for the team?

blocks.note: surface reading: a striker or star player who might score
setter's reading: the goal that levels the match, bringing the team back to parity

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a player; it is actually the goal that draws the scores level.
explanation.definitionFit: In football this is the goal that makes the score level, so it scores a point that may salvage a draw.

clue.text: Little animals endure for the most part dirty homes

indicators.note: for the most part keeps most of the word but drops its tail

explanation.surface: Small creatures putting up with squalid dwellings.
explanation.walkthrough: Beasties is a Scottish word, as in Burns's wee beastie.
explanation.definitionFit: Beasties are small creatures or insects, a Scots diminutive of beasts.

clue.text: Disorder in London thoroughfare, ending in trouble for area repeatedly

indicators.note: for means one letter takes the place of another in the street name
ending in picks out the final letter of the following word
repeatedly says the swap is made at every occurrence, not just once

blocks.note: Pall Mall, a street in St James's, London
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Chaos on a London street, with trouble breaking out again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Repeatedly means each A in PALL MALL becomes E. Pall Mall is a famous street of gentlemen's clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pell-mell means in a confused rush, so it conveys disorder or headlong chaos.

clue.text: Like chemical reaction bringing death to different chap shortly

indicators.note: shortly means the word for chap is cut short at its end

explanation.surface: A lab experiment that kills off another fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: An endothermal reaction absorbs heat from its surroundings, a chemistry term for heat-taking processes.

clue.text: Thus, inwardly deceived, gets married, beset by gloom?

indicators.note: inwardly says the next word goes inside the word for thus

blocks.note: to be had is to be fooled

explanation.surface: A deceived person marries, then sinks into depression.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadowed means darkened, overcast by shade, which the question mark extends to being surrounded by gloom.

clue.text: Troublesome head interferes, so play it cautiously

indicators.note: troublesome letters are unruly ones, and the words after it get thrown about

explanation.surface: A meddling boss getting in the way, so better be careful.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to choose the cautious course rather than risk a mistake, playing it safe.

clue.text: What actor finds difficult to learn? Bad luck!

definitions.text: What actor finds difficult to learn?

blocks.clueFragment: What actor finds difficult to learn?
blocks.note: first meaning: tricky passages of a script
second meaning: a British exclamation of sympathy

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation is old-fashioned British, said to commiserate with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally tricky speeches to memorise, and idiomatically a sympathetic interjection meaning tough luck.

clue.text: Excess praise is given to monarch returning

indicators.note: returning means the whole string written so far is read from its end back

explanation.surface: Too much flattery heaped on a returning king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Is appears twice: once as a letter piece, once in the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Residual describes what is left over, the remainder or surplus beyond what was used.

clue.text: Appeal for help and love just about acceptable?

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Calling for help and affection is barely good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means middling, neither good nor bad, only passable in quality.

clue.text: Most stupid old boy, American absorbed by cricket match?

indicators.note: absorbed by means the American is soaked up inside the match

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy

explanation.surface: Mocking an old fellow and a Yank engrossed in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match lasting several days.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow to understand, dull-witted, so the superlative is dimmest of all.

clue.text: Note placed on street that can attract a person's attention

definitions.text: that can attract a person's attention

blocks.note: postscript, a note at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A notice stuck on a street to catch passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is the whispered sound used to get somebody's notice quietly, an interjection.

clue.text: Rose admired strange animals in zoo?

indicators.note: strange letters are odd, unfamiliar ones, so they are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Rose was charmed by the exotic creatures at the zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Dromedaries are one-humped camels, the kind of large beast often kept in zoos.

clue.text: Make gear, nice clothes

indicators.note: clothes as a verb: the words wrap around the answer like a garment

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Instructions to sew some kit into nice outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: Clothes looks like a noun but is the verb, meaning covers.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to earn it, as in making a living or a profit.

clue.text: Hesitation about small smell that's providing a jog to the memory

definitions.text: providing a jog to the memory

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the sound of hesitating is written backwards

explanation.surface: Pausing over a faint aroma that brings back the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting picture: smell is famously the sense most tied to memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Reminiscent means bringing something to mind, suggestive of an earlier experience.

clue.text: After short time, removes restriction on police force

explanation.surface: A police force soon frees itself from regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: Mounties are the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Mounties is the familiar name for the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, Canada's national constabulary.

clue.text: Small room has power unit — there's hesitation to end trapped inside

indicators.note: trapped inside says the later pieces are held within the power unit

explanation.surface: A tiny room with a generator, and a pause before stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: Small room is a euphemism for the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A water closet is a flushing toilet, and the smallest room is a jokey name for the loo.

clue.text: Learner with book that describes a significant event

blocks.note: L for learner, as on L-plates
the Gospel of Mark, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A student holding a volume that records something momentous.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmark is a turning point or milestone, an occasion marking an important stage.

clue.text: Outdoor operator — one who takes …

blocks.note: first meaning: a surgeon whose patients grow outside, in parks and gardens
second meaning, read on into the next clue: a person who removes limbs from woody plants

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins the clue to the following one: the expert takes off what the next answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: An arborist who prunes and repairs trees, cutting off limbs, is called by this surgical title.

clue.text: Coppers in coloured glassware

explanation.surface: Pennies kept in tinted glass jars.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppers here means police officers, not coins; bluebottle is old British slang for a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebottle is dated slang for a police officer, from the blue uniform, so it means coppers.

clue.text: … this expands business

definitions.note: carries on from the clue before: what the tree expert takes off

blocks.note: first meaning: read on from the previous clue, what a tree expert removes from a trunk
second meaning: diversifies a firm into new areas

explanation.walkthrough: Read with the clue before it, the answer describes what the tree expert removes, and on its own means diversifies.
explanation.definitionFit: To do this is to extend activities into new fields, diversifying an enterprise into new markets.

clue.text: Bill's friend beginning to expect savagery, one denied kindness

indicators.note: beginning to picks out only the opening letter of the next word
denied means the numeral is refused entry and taken away

blocks.note: Bill and Ben, the Flowerpot Men of children's TV

explanation.surface: Bill's mate expected brutality but was shown gentleness.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Ben were puppet gardeners on a classic British children's programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Benevolence is goodwill and generosity toward others, a disposition to do good.

clue.text: Goes down, having lost heart, and fades away

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter is taken out

explanation.surface: Someone sinking, losing courage and wilting.
explanation.walkthrough: Goes down looks like the definition, but it is the word losing its middle V.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound or light that dies dwindles to nothing, fading out gradually.

clue.text: Hate a man unduly — becoming this?

definitions.text: Hate a man unduly — becoming this?

indicators.note: unduly suggests something improper, so the preceding letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Detesting a man excessively turns him into something loathed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: excessive hatred makes a man an object of loathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is something or someone detested, an object of intense dislike or a curse.

clue.text: Tease flighty creature, unkind female creating trouble

blocks.note: ill means harsh or unkind, as in ill will
Ate, the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Mocking a fickle, mean woman who causes strife.
explanation.walkthrough: Creating trouble describes Ate, the goddess who led people into folly.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite or arouse in a teasing, playful way.

clue.text: A number of chaps having drug injected by back-street accommodation

indicators.note: injected says the drug is pushed in between the number and the chaps
back says the abbreviation for street is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Ten men on drugs in housing down a side alley.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenements are large blocks of rented flats, a classic form of urban housing.

clue.text: Severely cut-down note is finished by editor

explanation.surface: A drastically pruned memo gets completed by the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: The is plays twice: as letters and in the link telling us the editor comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Minimised means reduced to the smallest possible amount, so drastically reduced.

clue.text: Beasts, those out of breath getting hot inside

indicators.note: inside says the hot letter goes into the middle of the breathless ones

blocks.note: H for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Breathless creatures overheating.
explanation.definitionFit: Panthers are big cats, wild beasts such as leopards or jaguars.

clue.text: Prison kids? They may grow up in a dank environment

definitions.text: They may grow up in a dank environment

explanation.surface: Children raised in jail, brought up somewhere damp.
explanation.walkthrough: Grow up is literal: these columns rise from a cave floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalagmites are mineral columns rising from the floors of damp caves as dripping water deposits calcium.

clue.text: Cunning form of winter transport arriving on time

explanation.surface: A sly winter vehicle turning up punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is craftiness or dexterity, as in sleight of hand, so trickery.

clue.text: Conservative resigning maybe or holding tight?

blocks.note: resigning is one way of leaving a post

explanation.surface: A Tory quitting office, or clinging on to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb cleave also means split, so the surface plays on its two opposite senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave to something is to cling to it firmly, so cleaving is clinging or holding tight.

clue.text: Girl trailing after dope in city

indicators.note: trailing after puts the girl's name behind the word for dope

blocks.note: information, as in the inside dope

explanation.surface: A girl following a drug dealer around a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope means information here, not drugs; gen is British slang for the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is the Swiss lakeside city, home to many international organisations.

clue.text: Crafty additional label — it gets missed

indicators.note: missed means left out, so the little pronoun is dropped

explanation.surface: A cunning extra tag that nobody notices.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtle can mean clever and cunning, artful in a quiet way, so sly.

clue.text: The Spanish form of therapy given examination with people voting

explanation.surface: A Spaniard undergoing treatment and a check-up among voters.
explanation.definitionFit: Electoral describes anything relating to elections, the process of citizens casting ballots.

clue.text: Bar charging nothing, beginning to end

indicators.note: the opening letter is shifted to the back of the word

explanation.surface: A pub serving drinks at no charge from opening to closing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar looks like a pub but means a sandbank or ridge in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or sand near the surface, as is a bar at a river mouth.

clue.text: Torch made of iron and gold carried by Mary's companion

indicators.note: carried by means the companion is held inside the metals

explanation.surface: A torch of precious metals borne by Mary's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The companion is from the nursery rhyme, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, especially one made of several thick wicks.

clue.text: Country fellow who peered over wall

blocks.note: first meaning: a nation in central Africa
second meaning: the cartoon face doodled peeking over a wall

explanation.walkthrough: Mr Chad was British wartime graffiti: a bald head and nose over a wall, captioned Wot no...?
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a landlocked African republic and the doodled character of wartime British graffiti.

clue.text: Good old-fashioned verses for operatic character

explanation.surface: Fine dated poetry written for a figure in opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Grimes is the fisherman antihero of Benjamin Britten's opera named after him.

clue.text: Complete the circle maybe to stay within budget?

blocks.note: first meaning, literal: join the two tips of a line into a loop
second meaning: to manage on one's income

explanation.walkthrough: Maybe flags that closing a loop is just one example of the literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have just enough money to cover your expenses, managing financially.

clue.text: Article by upright character, good person who believes in God

blocks.note: a saint is a good person

explanation.surface: An essay about a moral, God-fearing person.
explanation.walkthrough: Good person gives ST, a saint; the definition then starts at person.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist holds that God or gods exist, as opposed to an atheist.

clue.text: Group lying in grass, back to remember the good old days?

definitions.text: back to remember the good old days?

indicators.note: lying in means the group rests inside the plant word

explanation.surface: A band sprawled on the lawn, back together for nostalgia.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition pictures old friends or a band together again, reminiscing.
explanation.definitionFit: Reunited means brought back together after separation, as old friends or a band are.

clue.text: Situation in which bishops may have been done away with

definitions.text: Situation in which bishops may have been done away with

blocks.note: surface reading: a church upheaval in which clergy are got rid of

blocks.clueFragment: may have been done away with
blocks.note: setter's reading: chess pieces captured, leaving few on the board late in play

explanation.walkthrough: Bishops are chess pieces; late in a game many pieces have been taken.
explanation.definitionFit: The endgame is the final stage of a chess match, when most pieces have been exchanged off.
